results.route_rationale: EDAC-style critic diversity-penalty definition; check normalisation of the pairwise-gradient sum.

math_result.reasoning: The equation adds a diversity penalty to the value loss: α_div/(N−1) times the sum of pairwise inner products of action-gradients of the critic ensemble over ordered pairs i ≠ j. The ordered-pair count is N(N−1), so the penalty equals α_div·N·(average pairwise inner product). EDAC's original penalty instead divides by N(N−1) (a plain average), so the constant factor differs by N; however this is a free-coefficient design definition (α_div absorbs any constant), not a derivation, so it is not an error. The term ⟨∇ q_i, ∇ q_j⟩ is a well-defined scalar inner product. No algebraic error.

Main text §4.2 defines the unified actor loss as L_actor = β_q·L_q + β_BC·L_BC − β_H·H(π(·|s_t)) + β_div·L_div + β_dyn·L_dyn, explicitly stating that the critic diversity loss L_div and dynamics-model regularisation L_dyn are included with coefficients β_div and β_dyn. These two equations assert different formulas for the same quantity and therefore contradict each other. Since both are definitions (neither is a derived theorem), the defect is a definitional inconsistency requiring clarification rather than a broken derivation; it does not invalidate the empirical results (severity: minor).

results.route_rationale: Change-of-variables identity for a tanh-squashed Normal (log p(a) = log p(z) − log(1 − a²)); standard and checkable by inspection.

math_result.reasoning: For a = tanh(z) the change-of-variables formula gives p_A(a) = p_Z(z) / |da/dz| with da/dz = sech²(z) = 1 − tanh²(z) = 1 − a². Hence log p_A(a) = log p_Z(z) − log(1 − a²), which is exactly what the code computes (the +1e-6 is a numerical-stability constant; since a ∈ (−1,1), 1 − a² > 0 and no absolute value is needed). This is the standard tanh-squash density correction and is correct.

The result $\hat{v}_{t+1}$ must be scalar because it is squared inside the value loss (Eq 6).

The appendix defines the unified actor loss as $\mathcal{L}_{\text{actor}} = \beta_q \mathcal{L}_q + \beta_{\text{BC}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{BC}} - \beta_{\mathcal{H}} \mathcal{H}(\pi(\cdot|s_t))$ and states it 'consists of' three terms, while main text §4.2 defines the same $L_{\text{actor}}$ with two additional terms $+ \beta_{\text{div}} L_{\text{div}} + \beta_{\text{dyn}} L_{\text{dyn}}$. The two equations assert different formulas for the same quantity — a definitional contradiction.

summary: Verified the mathematical content of 'A Clean Slate for Offline RL' (13 self-contained equations; the paper states no theorems, lemmas, or proofs). 12 snippets were routed to informal review (verify-math) and 1 to formal verification (verify-math-lean). Lean machine-checked the only genuinely formalisable non-trivial claim — the Decision-Transformer return-to-go recursion R̂_{t+1} = R̂_t − r_t following from R̂_t = ∑_{t'=t}^{T} r_{t'} — and PASSED it (compiles clean, no sorry/sorryAx, axioms are the standard propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), confirming that recursion is correct. The remaining snippets are definitions of losses and targets (expected return, unified actor loss, value target, value/critic/actor losses, BC/AWR variants, MOPO penalised reward, tanh-squash log-probability); all are well-formed except two minor defects: (1) Eq (5) adds the action-space vector α_BC·(ã−a) to the scalar value target v_{t+1}, which is ill-typed as printed for multi-dimensional action spaces; and (2) the appendix Eq (8) defines L_actor with three terms while main text §4.2 defines the same symbol with five terms (omitting β_div·L_div and β_dyn·L_dyn). Both findings are minor (they concern appendix/unified-framework definitions, not the paper's empirical results), yielding verdict MINOR_ERRORS at confidence 0.75. The shared Lean project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper pre-existed this run (created by an earlier verification session), was reused rather than re-created, and is left in place (lean_project_kept: true); the proof was saved to Paper/Verified/paper__EQUATION__3.lean.
